research_page.title: FINGER Trial Protocol: Multi-domain lifestyle intervention
research_page.description: Registry protocol for the landmark FINGER trial testing a 2-year multi-domain lifestyle intervention to prevent cognitive decline.
research_page.authors_line_md: Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare
research_page.takeaway_md: The FINGER trial protocol established the framework for testing whether a combination of nutritional guidance, exercise, cognitive training, and vascular risk monitoring can prevent cognitive decline. While this registry record lacks data, the protocol laid the foundation for landmark peer-reviewed findings demonstrating the efficacy of multi-domain lifestyle interventions in at-risk older adults.
key_findings_md: The registry record outlines a 2-year intervention comparing multi-domain lifestyle counseling to standard health counseling (ClinicalTrials.gov).
The primary prespecified endpoint was cognitive impairment measured by a Neuropsychological Test Battery (NTB), Stroop, and Trail Making tests (ClinicalTrials.gov).
Although the registry indicates 'Results posted: false', subsequent peer-reviewed publications reported significant cognitive benefits (Clinical-trials researcher).
research_page.methods_md: Interventional, randomized, single-blind trial aiming to enroll 1,200 older adults (aged 60-77) with an elevated dementia risk (Dementia Risk Score >= 6) and specific cognitive deficits. The primary intervention phase lasted 2 years. Registered as NCT01041989.
research_page.trial_evidence_md: The FINGER protocol represents a foundational proof-of-concept in dementia prevention. Although the ClinicalTrials.gov record is poorly maintained (listed as 'Unknown' status with no results posted), the [FINGER trial](/trials/finger-nct01041989) was successfully completed and read out in 2015, showing that multi-domain interventions significantly preserve cognitive function. This success spawned the World-Wide FINGERS network and directly inspired replication studies like the [US-POINTER trial](/trials/us-pointer-nct03688126).
research_page.sentiment_md: Public sentiment regarding the FINGER protocol and lifestyle interventions is predominantly hopeful, particularly in tech and science communities that emphasize actionable, non-pharmacological prevention. However, media hype often oversimplifies the evidence, conflating the modest slowing of cognitive decline in asymptomatic, at-risk individuals with a 'cure' for established Alzheimer's disease. Caregiver communities remain notably quiet on the protocol, often expressing exhaustion over unsolicited lifestyle advice for patients who are already severely impaired.
caveats_md: This document is a prospective registry protocol, not a peer-reviewed paper, and contains no empirical results or data.
The clinical registry record is officially abandoned or poorly maintained, showing an 'Unknown' status despite the trial completing its primary phase in 2013.
Public discourse frequently loses the vital nuance that this intervention aims to slow cognitive decline in 'at-risk' populations, not reverse established clinical dementia.
relates_to_md: [US-POINTER Trial](/trials/us-pointer-nct03688126) — A major US-based replication and adaptation of the FINGER lifestyle intervention protocol.
[MET-FINGER Trial](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05109169) — An ongoing study investigating the combination of the FINGER lifestyle protocol with pharmacological treatment (metformin).

trial_pages.title: FINGER
trial_pages.description: A 2-year multi-domain lifestyle intervention to prevent cognitive impairment in at-risk older adults.
trial_pages.drug: Multi-domain lifestyle intervention (nutrition, exercise, cognitive training, vascular monitoring)
trial_pages.sponsor: Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare
trial_pages.population: Adults aged 60-77 years with elevated dementia risk (CAIDE score >= 6) and cognition at or slightly below average for age
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Cognitive impairment assessed with a Neuropsychological Test Battery (NTB), and Stroop and Trail Making tests over 2 years
trial_pages.why_md: The FINGER trial was designed to answer whether a comprehensive, multi-domain lifestyle intervention could prevent or delay cognitive decline in older adults at elevated risk for dementia. It serves as a foundational proof-of-concept for non-pharmacological [prevention](/research) strategies.
status_log_md: **2015-06-06** — Primary 2-year results published in [The Lancet](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)60461-5), demonstrating significant cognitive benefits.
trial_pages.results_md: At 2 years, the multidomain intervention significantly improved cognitive functioning compared to the control group (between-group difference in NTB total Z score change of 0.022 per year, p=0.030), establishing the efficacy of combination lifestyle modifications.

trial_pages.title: US-POINTER
trial_pages.description: A 2-year structured multi-domain lifestyle intervention for older adults at risk of cognitive decline.
trial_pages.population: Adults aged 60-79 years at risk of cognitive decline with a sedentary lifestyle and suboptimal diet
trial_pages.why_md: US-POINTER tests whether the successful lifestyle interventions pioneered by the [FINGER trial](/trials/finger-nct01041989) can be adapted and replicated in a diverse American population, answering whether structured lifestyle coaching outperforms self-guided approaches.
status_log_md: **2025-08-26** — Primary results published in [JAMA](https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2025.12923), confirming structured lifestyle interventions improve global cognition.
trial_pages.results_md: A structured multidomain intervention produced a statistically significant, greater improvement in global cognition over 2 years compared to an unstructured, self-guided intervention (difference of 0.029 SD/year, p=0.008).

timeline_entries.title: 2015-06 — FINGER trial demonstrates lifestyle intervention slows cognitive decline
timeline_entries.body_md: Primary results from the [FINGER trial](/trials/finger-nct01041989) are published in The Lancet, providing landmark proof-of-concept that a multi-domain lifestyle intervention can preserve cognitive function in at-risk older adults.

timeline_entries.title: 2025-08 — US-POINTER trial replicates FINGER lifestyle benefits
timeline_entries.body_md: The [US-POINTER trial](/trials/us-pointer-nct03688126) publishes results in JAMA, confirming that structured lifestyle interventions improve global cognition in a diverse American population, successfully replicating the FINGER model.

notes_for_editor: The ClinicalTrials.gov record for NCT01041989 is officially marked 'Unknown' status with 'Results posted: false', but it is a highly famous completed trial (published in The Lancet in 2015). I have manually overridden the trial badge to 'Completed' to reflect reality, but noted the poor registry maintenance in the fact check and caveats.
